scope: Generic implementation acceptance index; design narrative is maintained separately

requirements.requirement: Use Pydantic, PyArrow, DataFusion, NetworkX and deltalake with distinct responsibilities and one logical model.
Retain SQLite as a credible transactional alternative; justify the selected stack by types, revisions and interoperability rather than size.
Persist a typed relational core, not only JSON node/edge bags.
Preserve element/model/type identities, independent names and readable aliases.
Give relationships their own identities and explicit type registry with direction, endpoints, cardinality and traversal rules.
Store canonical relationship directions and derive inverse views instead of maintaining duplicate inverses.
Add typed interface, deployment, data-schema, behavior, requirement and notation details only when fields or constraints justify them.
Represent multi-party handoffs/interactions as first-class objects with typed participants.
Link evidence and decisions to elements, relationships, fields or releases without building a second evidence platform.
Nest owned values; normalize independently identified and shared objects.
Keep the explicit interface Arrow schema and its foreign references as an implementation example.
Use the tested Arrow/Delta/DataFusion type intersection, explicit nullability and UTC microsecond instants; avoid baseline unions and extension types.
Use small namespaced extensions only as an escape hatch; promote frequently queried meaning into typed fields.
Use strict Pydantic domain validation and explicit Arrow mappings; validate cross-record architecture independently.
Use DataFusion for relational queries, comparisons and tabular validation; qualify recursive SQL where needed.
Construct disposable NetworkX projections from release-selected records; return typed/Arrow results.
Implement named traversal policies and retain paths, versions and evidence; do not equate reachability with certain failure.
Keep domain mutation separate from queries; use bound scalar SQL parameters or expressions.
Distinguish source history, storage history and architectural history.
Do not equate a Delta table version with an architecture release or claim native multi-table atomicity.
Publish an immutable manifest pinning every required table version, schema/profile version, source digest and artifact.
Start with full snapshots of changed tables, reuse unchanged versions and avoid replay-based micro-edit event sourcing.
Use one writer, a publication lock and an expected-parent check; stage and read back before exposing a release.
Permit orphan staged versions after failure, but never publish partial architecture state.
Retain referenced Delta history and create self-contained milestone Parquet/manifest/schema/source/output archives.
Record semantic change sets with rationale, authorship, decisions, field-level changes, validation and impact.
Hash canonical semantic content, preserving ordered sequences; distinguish layout changes; keep CDF supplementary.
Give design alternatives separate scenario/model identities and baseline references.
Separate design disposition, implementation, qualification, client acceptance and evidence/review status.
Model BPMN behavior, UML ordering, ERD keys/cardinality and notation bindings explicitly; do not infer them from generic edges.
Separate semantic and layout versions and the four meanings of validation success.
Use ruamel.yaml, Jinja2, lxml, pytest, Hypothesis and ty for their bounded roles; use the standard library for ordinary utilities.
Exclude overlapping dataframe, database, orchestration and ORM layers initially; do not import the whole pilot ontology stack.
Isolate Delta/DataFusion registration, retain a pinned-snapshot PyArrow fallback and normalize arro3 boundaries.
Keep application code Python-only, with one package/locked environment and no change to the separate book-library environment.
Keep narrative/decisions in Notion, executable permitted inputs in GitHub, compiled Delta local and dated exports in Dropbox.
Pin source revisions and digests, or authorized snapshots when immutable source versions are unavailable.
Expose baseline/change/validate/diff/review/persist/publish/output operations through a small API and CLI.
Start without partitioning, Z-ordering, elaborate compaction or custom indexes; rebuild the query catalog from the manifest.
Qualify round trips, same-release queries, semantic changes, interrupted publication, stale parents and historical schema migration.
Preserve unknowns, manual processes and evidence gaps; do not invent facts to satisfy structural checks.
Do not claim tested interoperability; retain immutable Parquet plus manifests as the simpler alternative.
